fields.h1: Build Airline Survey Questions for Each Stage of a Flight
fields.hero_description: Build airline survey questions that rate every stage of the trip and ask delay questions only when the flight landed late.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an Airline Survey
fields.features_subheading: One prompt builds the questions and the table every answer lands in. A follow-up prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_1:
A rating for each stage of the trip

List the stages to score, such as booking, check-in, boarding, the cabin, and arrival. Emergent drafts a 1 to 5 rating and a comment box for each, and a prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that depend on what happened

The app reads each flight's arrival time and bag reports from your operations system through its API. A passenger who landed on time never sees a question about a delay.
fields.feature_3:
Flight number and route on every answer

Each response is a row in a database you own, stamped with the flight number, route, date, and seat. Filter boarding scores by airport or compare one route month over month.
fields.feature_4:
Low scores sent to the person who can act

Pick a score that needs a reply and who gets it. The app sends a Slack message or an email to that person, such as a station manager, with the flight and the comment attached.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Passengers answer one question per screen on a phone, at the baggage carousel or in a taxi. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so every passenger on a full flight can answer.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, with the code on GitHub

Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep each version of the questions.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Airlines Use Their Survey Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
Boarding came last for LW 418, with 31 of 96 votes

Larchwick Air sends one survey per flight after landing, rating each stage from booking to arrival and asking which was worst. On flight LW 418 from Denver to Boise, 96 of 142 passengers answered, and 31 of the 96 named boarding. Station manager Thandie Vesper moved the Denver gate to zone boarding.
fields.tab_content_2:
After a late landing, 3 delay questions appear

Harrow Bay Airlines adds 3 delay questions when a flight lands 15 minutes or more past schedule. Flight HB 227 landed 2 hours 10 minutes late, and 33 of the 54 passengers who answered first heard about the delay at the gate. Ops lead Gideon Strand now sends the delay text when a new time is set.
fields.tab_content_3:
Bag scores of 1 or 2 go to the baggage lead

Dunmarsh Air surveys each passenger whose bag arrived late, once the bag is delivered. A delivery score of 1 or 2 out of 5 sends baggage lead Tobias Fenn a Slack message. Ines Rotherwood scored hers 1 because the bag went to the wrong hotel, and Tobias called her with the file in front of him.
fields.tab_content_4:
Portland got 512 votes before a seat was sold

Brightridge Air asks loyalty members in Tucson which of 4 new nonstop routes they would book, before it sells a ticket. Of the 1,240 members who answered, 512 chose Portland and 388 chose Austin. Network planner Nerys Drummond put Portland on the spring schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Airline Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write airline survey questions that rate each stage, branch for delays and bags, and tag answers by flight.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the stages of the trip
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Rate every stage on one scale
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Branch for delays and late bags
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start from the trip, not a template. List the stages a passenger moves through on your airline, from the booking page to the arrival gate. Put that list in your prompt, and Emergent drafts one rating question for each stage.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use the same 1 to 5 scale for every stage. Then boarding and the cabin compare on one flight and across months. After the ratings, ask one open question: which stage was worst, and why? That answer shows where to look first.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The Bureau of Transportation Statistics counts a flight as late when it arrives or departs 15 minutes or more after the scheduled time. Use the same line for your delay questions, and show bag questions only to passengers who reported a late bag.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the core survey near 10 questions. A passenger should be able to finish it at the baggage carousel. Ask about the flight they just took. Save questions about travel habits and future routes for a separate survey to loyalty members.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tag every answer with the flight
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which flight details each answer carries before launch. With the flight and seat attached, comments become a query: every boarding score from one gate, or every cabin comment from one aircraft type in a month.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide who hears about a low score
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the score that needs a reply, such as anything under 3 out of 5, and name one person for each kind of problem. A baggage complaint goes to the baggage lead, and a boarding complaint goes to the station manager for that airport.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on one route first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the survey on one route for a week before adding the rest. Read the answers as they come in, reword any question passengers skip or misread, and then turn on the delay and bag branches for every flight.

faq_plan.a: Airline survey questions are the questions an airline asks passengers about a trip they just took: check-in, boarding, the seat, the crew, and what happened after landing, plus follow-ups for a delay or a late bag. Airlines also ask them before a route launches, to see which destinations members would book.

faq_plan.q: How do I create airline survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the stages to rate and when delay or bag questions should appear. Emergent builds the survey and its database, and a follow-up prompt changes any question before the first flight goes out.

faq_plan.q: How many airline survey questions should one survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Aim for about 10 in the core survey: a rating per stage, one question on the worst stage, and a comment box. Delay and bag questions add length only for the passengers they apply to. A passenger whose flight went fine never sees them.

faq_plan.q: Can airline survey questions be lighthearted without losing useful answers?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in small doses. One playful question near the end, such as which snack should come back, keeps the tone friendly and leaves the ratings alone. Keep the stage ratings plain. For a survey written entirely for fun, these funny survey questions are a better starting point.

faq_plan.q: When should airline survey questions go out after a flight lands?
faq_plan.a: Send it within a few hours of landing, while the trip is fresh, and send one per flight. For a late bag, wait until the bag is delivered, or the passenger rates a delivery that has not happened. Emergent builds that timing into the app, which waits for each flight's arrival time before the survey goes out.

faq_plan.q: Should delayed passengers get different airline survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A passenger whose flight landed 15 minutes or more late has a different trip to report: when they first heard about the delay, whether the new time held, and how rebooking went. Ask those 3 questions only to them, and keep the stage ratings the same for everyone.

faq_plan.q: Should airline survey questions use rating scales or yes or no answers?
faq_plan.a: Use both, for different jobs. A 1 to 5 scale shows how good a stage was, while a yes or no question settles a fact, such as whether the gate announced the delay. For a survey built mostly on the second kind, see this yes no questions survey.

faq_plan.q: How do I tag answers to airline survey questions with the flight and seat?
faq_plan.a: Pass the flight number and seat into each passenger's survey link. Every answer then arrives tagged, and the passenger never types a flight number. Emergent keeps those answers in a database you own, ready to filter by route or by gate.

faq_plan.q: Should answers to airline survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Not if you want to reply to complaints. A low baggage score helps only when someone can call the passenger back. Say in the invitation that answers are tied to the booking, and add an optional comment box the passenger can leave unsigned.

faq_plan.q: Where does a recommend question fit among airline survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Put it last, after the stage ratings: "How likely are you to recommend us to a friend or colleague?" scored on a zero-to-ten scale. That is the Net Promoter question. Compare the answers by route. For the full setup and scoring, see this nps survey guide.
